question.text: SEBI regulations require that Direct Plans must have which of the following characteristics compared to Regular Plans of the same scheme?

answer.text: A lower Total Expense Ratio (TER) because distribution expenses/commission are excluded and no commission is paid out of the Direct Plan
A higher minimum investment amount to compensate for the absence of distributor services
A separate fund manager and investment strategy optimized for cost-conscious investors
A mandatory lock-in period of 1 year since the investor has no distributor to guide early redemption

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A (p.166), Direct Plans shall have a lower expense ratio than Regular Plans because distribution expenses/commission are excluded, and no commission is paid out of Direct Plans. Per p.177, the Regular Plan expense ratio is higher because distribution costs are accounted for in it. Per p.106, the TERs of both plans are disclosed. The Trap: Option B is wrong — there is no higher minimum investment requirement for Direct Plans. Option C is a critical misconception — both plans share the same fund manager, investment strategy, and portfolio. Option D fabricates a lock-in period that does not exist for Direct Plans. Note: Because Direct Plans carry a lower TER, their NAV diverges over time from the corresponding Regular Plan NAV, even though the underlying portfolio is identical.
